items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Jelly came with his orchestra... I remember that one of the trumpet players was the funniest looking red head... I felt sorry for Jelly

ctx.x: The dance finished around 2 or 2.30 a.m. and we were a real happy bunch of fellows that piled into Helvey's model T Ford and headed for home. But the morning was not as pleasant coming home as it had been when we were going to Dayton because half way back, the motor started knocking. The only thing that Helvey knew about the car was how to drive it and the rest of us didn't know that much. Eventually there was no power in the motor and we managed to go to Woodlawn Inn where Helvey called a taxi and we arrived in…

When "Jelly Roll" Morton came to Cincinnati with Fate Marable, he was telling everyone whose ear he could catch, that he was going to bring an orchestra to town that would wash Fate Marable's band away. So a few months later, Jelly came with his orchestra and to make a long story short, it was the worst sounding band I had ever heard. Where Jelly got those musicians, only the Lord and Jelly know. I remember that one of the trumpet players was the funniest looking red head, yellow complexioned person I had ever…

Eventually some record of a band known as Fletcher Henderson of New York reached Cincy and the first one I heard was at Edgar James's house. On one side of the record was a number called "Money Blues" with a great trumpet solo. Later I found out that the name of the soloist was a man called Louis Armstrong. This was without doubt the greatest trumpet solo I had ever heard, and I bought the record as soon as I could find a copy.
